title: project export lowercases APEXlang file and folder names
workaround: Run `apex export -applicationid <id> -exptype APEXLANG -dir src/database/<schema>/apex_apps/f<id> -f` after `project export`.
prompt: Remove the exported application folder, run `project export -o APEX.<app_id>` in the test repo, and compare every mixed-case file or folder name of the baseline export with the exported names.
successCriteria: Every mixed-case name in the baseline export (for example static-files/img/mixedCaseImageName.webp) is exported with the same case.

title: project export corrupts binary APEX static files
workaround: Run `apex export -applicationid <id> -exptype APEXLANG -dir src/database/<schema>/apex_apps/f<id> -f` after `project export`; it rewrites the binary files correctly.
prompt: Remove the exported application folder, run `project export -o APEX.<app_id>` in the test repo, and compare each binary file of the baseline export (static-files icons and images) byte for byte with the exported file.
successCriteria: Every binary file is byte-identical to the baseline (same SHA-1).

title: project export keeps files of APEX components deleted in APEX
workaround: Delete src/database/<schema>/apex_apps/f<id> before `project export`, or run `apex export -applicationid <id> -exptype APEXLANG -dir src/database/<schema>/apex_apps/f<id> -f` after it.
prompt: Start from the baseline export. Install a copy of the APEXlang source without page 100 (`apex validate` + `apex import`) so the page is deleted in APEX, then run `project export -o APEX.<app_id>` WITHOUT removing the export folder. Check whether the page 100 file is still in the folder the export wrote pages into. Also check that `apex export ... -f` removes it. Finally re-import the baseline source to restore page 100.
successCriteria: After project export, the export folder contains no file for page 100 (p00100-*.apx).

title: project export -o does not export synonyms
workaround: Export the synonym together with its table (`project export -o <table>`) or run a full `project export`.
prompt: Create table REG_004_T and synonym REG_004_SYN for it in the project schema, run `project export -o REG_004_SYN`, and look for synonyms/reg_004_syn.sql. If it is missing, run `project export -o REG_004_T` as a control: the synonym is exported along with its table, which proves it is exportable. Drop both objects and restore src afterwards.

title: APEXlang source written by project export fails apex validate
oracleStatus: not reported separately (consequence of the lowercasing bug, 001)
workaround: Run `apex export -applicationid <id> -exptype APEXLANG -dir src/database/<schema>/apex_apps/f<id> -f` after `project export`.
prompt: Export the application with `project export -o APEX.<app_id>` into an empty apex_apps folder and run `apex validate -input <folder with application.apx>`. The lowercased static file name no longer matches the reference in static-files.apx, so APEXlang compilation reports REFERENCE_NOT_FOUND.
successCriteria: `apex validate` on the exported APEXlang folder prints `Validation successful`.

title: Readable-mode project export flattens APEXlang into f<app_id>
prompt: With apex.apexlang not set (readable mode), export the application into an empty apex_apps folder and find application.apx. It must sit in a subfolder of f<app_id> (documented: f<app_id>/<alias>/; Oracle intends f<app_id>/readable/), not directly in f<app_id> beside f<app_id>.sql.
successCriteria: application.apx is in a subfolder of src/database/<schema>/apex_apps/f<app_id>/.

title: project export -o APEX.<id> exports users and data that were not requested
prompt: Restore src to the baseline, run `project export -o APEX.<app_id>`, and list every file changed or added under src outside the application folder (git diff against the baseline tag plus untracked files). Seen with any -o export in SQLcl 26.2.2 (e.g. -o <package> also exported 14 users), not only APEX applications.

title: project stage refuses the APEX controller generated by an earlier SQLcl version
prompt: On a branch from the baseline (staged by SQLcl 26.1), delete a page in APEX, export the application, commit, and run `project stage`. Stage must regenerate dist/releases/apex/f<app_id>/f<app_id>.xml instead of stopping with "has been edited and stage will not overwrite it automatically".

title: Switching to APEXlang mode leaves the legacy SQL controller in apex.changelog.xml
workaround: Remove the legacy dist/releases/apex/f<id> folder and its <include> from apex.changelog.xml by hand.
prompt: On a branch from the baseline, run `project config set -name apex.apexlang -value true`, export the application into an empty apex_apps folder, commit, run `project stage`, and read the <include> entries of dist/releases/apex/apex.changelog.xml.
successCriteria: apex.changelog.xml no longer includes f<app_id>/f<app_id>.xml once the APEXlang controller is added.

title: project export exports ORDS of the connected user instead of the project schemas
workaround: None with a deployer connection; export ORDS while connected as (or proxied to) the schema owner.
prompt: The baseline REST-enables the project schema and defines module regression.dept (custom changeset). Restore src to the baseline, run `project export -debug` with the deployer connection, and search src/database/<schema> for the module name. The debug log shows `ORA-20012: Schema not REST enabled : <connected user>` from ords_export.export_schema() called without a schema.
successCriteria: An exported .sql file under src/database/<schema>/ contains the ORDS module regression.dept.

title: project stage regenerates ORDS changesets even when ORDS did not change
workaround: Discard the regenerated dist/releases/ords/<schema>/ords.sql before committing.
prompt: Needs the ORDS export of the project schema in src (src/database/<schema>/ords/...), which `project export` with a deployer connection cannot produce while 011 is open. With such a baseline: on a branch, change one non-ORDS object (e.g. add a column to a REG_012_* table), export it, commit, run `project stage`, and check whether dist/releases/ords/<schema>/ords.sql (or any ORDS changeset) is written although no ORDS metadata changed. Repeat with ORDS_SCHEMA excluded in project.filters.
successCriteria: project stage writes no ORDS files when ORDS metadata did not change.

title: project export appends a semicolon to a view's trailing line comment
workaround: Edit the exported view file and remove the semicolon from the comment line.
prompt: Create view REG_013_V whose query ends with a line comment (`from dept -- reg_013 trailing line comment`), run `project export -o REG_013_V`, and read the comment line in the exported file. SQLcl 25.3.2 wrote `-- reg_013 trailing line comment;` followed by a separate `;`. Drop the view afterwards.
successCriteria: The exported comment line does not end with a semicolon; the statement terminator is on its own line.
